title: Freshness checks must read ExternalDataSchema.last_run_at, never last_synced_at alone; don't advance last_synced_at on zero-row runs
answers: why is last_synced_at not updated when a sync imports nothing
how do I tell when a warehouse schema last ran
schema shows stale / stopped syncing but jobs run on schedule
should I advance last_synced_at on a zero-batch v3 run
body:
Invariant: `last_synced_at` is also the signals watermark (`partition_field > last_synced_at`). The v3 pipeline deliberately does not advance it on a run that extracts zero rows (`pipeline_v3/pipeline.py:PipelineV3._stamp_full_run` writes only `sync_type_config.last_full_run_at`). If it did advance, rows arriving late with a partition value between two quiet runs would never emit a signal. That is why #104604 rejected the change and this PR kept that decision.
Which stamp each kind of run moves: a run that loads rows moves both stamps. A v3 zero-row run moves only `last_full_run_at`. A fast return on a negative probe moves only `last_synced_at`.
So any check that asks "when did a sync last run" (stale warnings, stall detection) must use `products/warehouse_sources/backend/models/external_data_schema.py:ExternalDataSchema.last_run_at`, which is the max of both. If you read only `last_synced_at`, a schema whose source is simply quiet gets reported as stalled or stale.
Use `ExternalDataSchema.last_full_run` to parse `last_full_run_at`. It returns None for a string that does not parse or has no timezone, so a naive stamp never counts as fresh. `create_job_model.py:_fast_return_eligible` and `sync_status.py:_is_stale` both use these properties. Don't hand-roll the parsing again.
applies: Any data-warehouse code that judges sync freshness or writes sync timestamps on ExternalDataSchema
